reasoning: A hybrid strategy is chosen because autonomous reasoning can quickly identify shared patterns in the instances' features, while XAI tools provide quantitative, model-agnostic attribution scores to validate which features have high influence despite lacking semantic relevance. This combination ensures both qualitative insight and robust, data-driven confirmation of spurious feature impacts.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 14962) and note their values and consistency across instances.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features (e.g., education=HS-grad, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) and their consistent values

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) are semantically relevant to income prediction or could be spurious indicators due to co-occurrence with other patterns.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned assessment of whether the shared features are semantically meaningful or potentially spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP and Integrated Gradients provide feature-level attribution scores that highlight which features drive predictions, even when semantically uninformative. LIME helps validate local interpretability, and sensitivity analysis quantifies the feature's impact when removed, confirming spuriousness. The intersection mode in SHAP ensures we focus on features with high importance across all misclassified instances, identifying potential spurious correlations.
